sources.title: National Register of Historic Places listings in downtown Denver
List of public art in Denver
Wikipedia GeoSearch sweep, 3 km around downtown Denver (200 geotagged articles)

stops.name: Colorado State Capitol
stops.description: Three separate markers on the west steps each claim the one-mile elevation, the leftovers of two resurveys, and the dome above them is covered in real gold leaf.

stops.name: Voorhies Memorial
stops.description: A 1919 triumphal arch closes the north end of Civic Center Park, fronted by a pond whose sea lion sculpture earned it the nickname Seal Pond.

stops.name: Denver City and County Building
stops.description: Denver's curved seat of government was finished in 1932 at the west end of Civic Center Park, deliberately squared off against the State Capitol at the other end.

stops.name: Denver Mint
stops.description: Striking coins since 1906 and now the single largest coin producer in the world, this is where the D mint mark on pocket change comes from.

stops.name: Denver Art Museum
stops.description: Gio Ponti's fortress-like 1971 building, the only design he ever completed in the United States, anchors a museum best known for its American Indian collection.

stops.name: Clyfford Still Museum
stops.description: A museum devoted to a single artist, holding about 93 percent of everything Clyfford Still made in his lifetime.

stops.name: History Colorado Center
stops.description: The state history museum opened here in 2012, one block south of the predecessor building that was torn down to make room for a courthouse.

stops.name: Denver Central Library
stops.description: Michael Graves gave the Denver Public Library's flagship its stack of mismatched postmodern volumes, sitting directly alongside the Art Museum.

stops.name: The Yearling
stops.description: Donald Lipski's pony perched on top of an enormous red chair has stood outside the Central Library since 1998.

stops.name: Molly Brown House
stops.description: The Capitol Hill home of Margaret Brown, the Titanic survivor the newspapers later rebranded as the Unsinkable Molly Brown.

stops.name: Brown Palace Hotel
stops.description: Frank Edbrooke's wedge-shaped hotel has been open since 1892 and was one of the first atrium hotels ever built.

stops.name: Paramount Theatre
stops.description: A 1930 movie palace turned concert hall that still plays one of the last two twin-console Wurlitzer theatre organs left in the country.

stops.name: Daniels & Fisher Tower
stops.description: Modeled on the campanile in Venice's Piazza San Marco, this 1910 tower was the tallest building between the Mississippi and California, and in 1918 a man free-climbed it in 38 minutes.

stops.name: Larimer Square
stops.description: Denver's oldest surviving commercial block, and the first stretch of the city to be named a historic district when it was saved from demolition in 1971.

stops.name: Denver Union Station
stops.description: The transportation hub at 17th and Wynkoop, where the historic station house now sits above a 22-gate underground bus terminal and a light rail platform.

note: Denver's first run. Chosen because it is the alphabetically first NFL host city that has never come up; nine cities have run so far (Atlanta, Baltimore, Boston, Buffalo, Charlotte, Chicago, Cincinnati, Cleveland, Dallas). 15 stops, all verified against their own articles. The walk is a Civic Center / Golden Triangle cluster, then north up the 16th Street Mall to LoDo; Capitol to Union Station is about 1.3 miles, so it is a long loop rather than a tight one, but every stop is in the downtown core. Voorhies Memorial is the only stop with no address or ZIP: it stands inside Civic Center Park and has no street number, and Nominatim resolves only to the W Colfax Ave frontage. Every other ZIP was looked up rather than assumed, which caught two wrong ones -- a street-level match put History Colorado Center in 80216 (Globeville) and the Central Library in 80274; querying by name instead of house number gave the correct 80203 and 80204. Dropped after reading the articles: the Christopher Columbus statue (torn down in 2020, now in storage), the Colorado History Museum (demolished 2010, superseded by History Colorado Center), Tabor Grand Opera House and Denham Theatre (both long demolished), and the Kit Carson figure from Pioneer Fountain (removed 2020, though the fountain itself still stands and could be added later). Denver Athletic Club was dropped as a private members' club. Deliberately left for a future batch, since this list was already at the top of the range: the Civic Center Park sculpture set (Bronco Buster, The Closing Era, On the War Trail, Civil War Monument, Liberty Bell, Armenian Khachkar), the Big Blue Bear at the Convention Center, Dancers at the Performing Arts Complex, Byers-Evans House, Cathedral Basilica of the Immaculate Conception, and the LoDo warehouse block around the Oxford Hotel and Barney L. Ford Building. Note that Denver already has roughly 37 waypoints in the table from earlier work, so expect a high In table rate on this batch.
